question: Should Crabbox support Jujutsu as a first-class workspace source, or support only an explicit Git-compatible revision/export path for jj repositories?
rationale: The current contract is intentionally Git-oriented, and choosing between native jj semantics and a narrower interoperability path affects CLI behavior, revision identity, caching, synchronization, and long-term maintenance.

options.title: Add a VCS adapter
options.body: Define a small workspace-source interface, preserve Git as the default implementation, and add native jj behavior with multi-parent fixtures and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Require explicit export
options.body: Support a documented command or option that makes users identify a Git-compatible commit or exported tree without teaching Crabbox native jj semantics.

options.title: Remain Git-only
options.body: Document jj as unsupported and provide a reliable workaround for producing a conventional Git checkout before running Crabbox.

recommendation.title: Add a VCS adapter
recommendation.body: Define a small workspace-source interface, preserve Git as the default implementation, and add native jj behavior with multi-parent fixtures and compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice changes the CLI's foundational repository model and therefore needs broad product and architecture ownership rather than an implementation-only decision.
